target_customer: Consumers who call or message people in other languages, with later interest from enterprises wanting live multilingual calls
problem: Language barriers make phone calls with family, friends and offshore teams hard, and existing translation waits for full sentences and loses the speaker's voice and emotion.
business_model: Consumer subscription app with an API and enterprise integrations

founders.name: Paddy Krishnamurthy
founders.background_notes: Also listed as Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy. The two founders met in college in Hong Kong.

founders.name: Amrutavarsh Kinagi
education: HKUST, BS computer science and math
previous_startups: Helen AI (lip-reading tool for the hearing impaired)
founders.background_notes: Speech AI researcher at Columbia; led robotics work on autonomous systems at HKUST.

technical_complexity.rationale: Streaming translation that does not wait for full sentences, on-the-fly voice cloning without enrollment and emotion transfer, over live phone calls, was research-adjacent and latency sensitive for a six person team.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary low-latency models gave a head start, but large platforms and foundation model vendors could build comparable translation and the consumer app had weak lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cisco acquired the company in November 2025 to bring voice-preserving translation into Webex, and the consumer apps were to close on December 15, 2025.

market_need_then: Advances in speech recognition, translation and voice synthesis made live speech-to-speech translation feasible around 2023, and multilingual calling to family and offshore teams was a clear consumer pain point.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain consumer language about talking to loved ones across languages

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage from TechCrunch and Slator at the seed launch; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch and trade press covered the launch, but the sources show no distinctive brand assets or community, and the name resembles many other dubbing tools.

outcome_analysis: EzDubs built low-latency voice-preserving translation, raised a $4.2M seed in December 2024, and sold to Cisco in November 2025 for Webex while shutting its consumer apps. The consumer product reached thousands of users but the exit was a technology and team purchase by an enterprise collaboration vendor. Deal terms were not disclosed.
